answerRecords.question: Tell us about an AI-powered product you have built or managed. What was your role, what AI technologies were used, and what product decisions did you personally own?
answerRecords.answer:
As Head of Computer Vision at DeepSight AI Labs, I led end-to-end delivery of production AI systems across mining, energy, banking, and retail - from scoping and architecture to model operations and on-site rollout. That experience shaped my focus on reliable, usable AI rather than impressive demos. ( technologies used: AWS, pytorch, python, docker, kubernetes etc )

recently I built a six-agent AI product that turns story ideas into illustrated, print-ready books. I owned the end-to-end. It used LLM agents and LangGraph-style orchestration.
aliases: Tell us about an AI-powered product you have built or managed. What was your role, what AI technologies were used, and what product decisions did you personally own?

answerRecords.question: Tell us about a product decision you got wrong, or that didn’t work out the way you expected. What happened, and what did you learn?
answerRecords.answer: For the Coal India project, we had a feature of tailgating that needed to be deployed, which was basically checking if the truck has another truck behind it while passing the boom barrier ( smuggling of Coal ) , we solved it with computer vision and AI models but soon realized that it was not enough as the smugglers used to turn away the camera from facing the boom barriers ( making the detector useless), so we had to develop camera fault and tamper feature for the cameras too. basically the product was first built just to solve the problem, but i failed to consider the human action in this case while designing at first.
aliases: Tell us about a product decision you got wrong, or that didn’t work out the way you expected. What happened, and what did you learn?

answerRecords.question: Tell me about a product or feature you owned from start to finish. What was your specific role, and what did you personally decide versus what the team decided?
answerRecords.answer: I have owned the delivery of numerous production computer-vision systems - including industrial safety analytics, monitoring, and large-scale exam proctoring ( ~10000 cameras per deployment) from customer problem definition through deployment. The team contributed implementation expertise, while I drove scope, architecture, trade-offs, rollout decisions and technical expertise when the team got stuck.
aliases: Tell me about a product or feature you owned from start to finish. What was your specific role, and what did you personally decide versus what the team decided?

answerRecords.question: Describe an enterprise deployment you led into production. What made it hard, and how did you de‑risk it?
answerRecords.answer:
As Head of Computer Vision at DeepSight AI Labs, I led end-to-end delivery of production AI systems across mining, energy, banking, and retail - from scoping and architecture to model operations and on-site rollout. 

One particular enterprise deployment would be for Coal India, where we had to make the cameras in coal mines intelligent by adding 7+ AI features per camera (~ 30 ) per site (5 different mines). It was hard, because we were a small team and the requirement was to make everything work on the edge itself ( economically ) and just relay the alerts to cloud. also to make it more difficult for us, the coal mafia used to turn the cameras away from the region of interests. 

so to solve the above we developed novel strategies to merge multiple datasets , models, created synthetic data to train our custom models and created features like tamper and camera fault ( so alerts are raised if someone turns the camera away from ROI )
aliases: Describe an enterprise deployment you led into production. What made it hard, and how did you de‑risk it?

answerRecords.question: What is the most impressive thing you’ve personally built or automated with AI? Describe exactly what you did, how it worked, and the measurable outcome
answerRecords.answer:
The most impressive thing would be, i improved the tamper algorithm making it 20x faster while being 10x more accurate and reduced the false postives compared to the previous Computer vision algorithms used for the feature. I swapped the CV algorithms with a AI model, that used contrastive loss to check the difference between frames and tell if it has been tampered. 

I have built many things, much more complex than this, but i like this because the solution was elegant, simple , quality improvement was massive, while solution was just a drop in replacement.
aliases: What is the most impressive thing you’ve personally built or automated with AI? Describe exactly what you did, how it worked, and the measurable outcome
